name: esp32
comment: The ESP32 (Xtensa LX6, two cores): 520 KB of SRAM and, on the modules this platform knows, 4 MB of external flash. Unlike an ARM part it has no single image: the bootloader, a partition table and the application are three binaries at three flash offsets.
comment_linker: The linker scripts, the memory map, the startup and the bootloader are ESP-IDF's, through the board's prelude: an ESP32 image needs the vendor's second-stage bootloader and its linker fragments, and a second copy of either is a second thing to keep in step with the silicon.

toolchain.comment: the compiler is named so CMake has one before `project()`; the prelude locates ESP-IDF and hands the build to it, and the flags, the linker fragments and the bootloader come from there

flash.comment: the ROM's own serial protocol over the board's USB-serial chip; the three binaries and their offsets come from what ESP-IDF built
